_comment: Technician review of the safety wording. `technician` stays null until a real, named, qualified person has reviewed the pages listed in `scope`; nothing here may be filled in to look diligent. When it is filled in, /sources/#review publishes the name, credentials, date and pages covered, and every safety page changes its notice from 'no technician review yet' to the reviewer's name and date. `scope` is a fallback only: the page list rendered on the site is derived from the data (every published page that carries an action plan), so it cannot drift from what is actually live.

technicianWhenPresent.name: Full name as the reviewer wants it published
technicianWhenPresent.credentials: e.g. ASE Master Automobile Technician, 12 years at an independent shop
technicianWhenPresent.credentialId: Certification number, if the reviewer agrees to publish it
pages: page slugs actually reviewed - a review covers pages, not the whole site
technicianWhenPresent.statement: One or two sentences in the reviewer's own words: what they checked, and what they did not.

scope: Every published page that renders a 'What to do now' action plan - the brake and ABS / warning-light symptom pages, plus the can-I-keep-driving trouble codes.

aiRecheck.by: AI-assisted review (automated evidence-consistency audit; not a human technician)
aiRecheck.method: Each action-plan row traced to its Grade-A source; level validity (stop/now/soon/ok); no conflicting levels for the same condition; hub.verdict cross-checked against rendered rows; render-side spot-checked in the build output.
aiRecheck.result: consistent — 10/10 pages: every row grounded in a Grade-A source, levels valid, no internal contradictions, hub.verdict matches the action plan.
aiRecheck.limitations: The stop-driving instruction is grounded only in the Toyota owner's manual we verified; other makes are not asserted to stop. This is a document-consistency check, not a hands-on mechanical judgment, and does not replace a licensed technician's opinion on a specific vehicle.
aiRecheck.note: An AI re-check raises confidence in the wording but is explicitly not a substitute for a qualified technician's review.

criteria: A current, verifiable automotive credential (ASE certification or equivalent), named and dated.
Review of the condition -> action rows, not of the specification figures: the question is whether the instruction is right for the condition, not whether a number was transcribed correctly.
Disagreement is published, not smoothed over: where the reviewer would word a row differently, the page says so.
The reviewer is named. An anonymous review is not published as a review.
